title: Preregistered Paired Evaluation of a Deterministic Verifier Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configuration Changes — Non‑informative Result under Shared‑Generation Semantics
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (cand-2026-01-prereg-v1) that tested whether deterministic verifier augmentation (generate → deterministic_netops_validator_v5 → optional repair) reduces the rate of verifier‑detected unsafe intent→configuration proposals produced by a hosted LLM. Design: N=200 preregistered unique intent→configuration tasks in a paired design comparing (a) baseline LLM‑only and (b) guarded pipeline (gpt-5-mini + deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (one LLM call per task) producing model_calls_used = 200. Observed (adversarial cluster): baseline SAFE = 200/200; guarded SAFE = 200/200 (paired contingency n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0). Estimated paired SAFE‑rate difference = 0.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Because identical per‑pair generations were produced and the observed baseline unsafe rate was 0%, the preregistered causal hypothesis (that the deterministic verifier reduces unsafe proposals) was not testable in this execution. We publish the complete preregistered run and artifacts, provide an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of testability failure, and give concrete, archive‑supported recommendations (independent per‑arm generation budgeting, adversarial injection calibration, and exploratory ROC reserves) for informative repeats.

sections.introduction: Automating human‑intent → device‑configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) promises to reduce operator effort and speed maintenance but introduces operational risk when generated changes are incorrect or unsafe. A widely proposed mitigation is tool‑augmentation: couple an LLM generator to deterministic validators, sandboxed simulators, or constrained executors in a generate–validate–repair pipeline so that proposed changes are checked before execution. We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (cand-2026-01-prereg-v1) to measure whether adding a deterministic validator causally reduces verifier‑detected unsafe proposals from a hosted LLM under controlled benign/adversarial prompt clusters. The preregistered estimand was the paired SAFE‑rate difference (guarded minus baseline) tested with an exact McNemar two‑sided procedure and paired bootstrap CIs. The executed run produced a ceiling outcome (all sampled candidates were SAFE in both arms), rendering the preregistered causal test non‑informative. This manuscript presents (1) the preregistered, fully archived run; (2) an artifact‑grounded diagnosis explaining why the confirmatory test was uninformative; and (3) concrete, artifact‑supported design recommendations for informative repeats that preserve preregistration integrity.
sections.related_work: Surveys and prototype reports document rapid adoption of LLMs for NetOps tasks (intent translation, configuration synthesis, diagnosis and limited remediation) while flagging safety and verification needs. Prior work shows that tool‑augmentation—pairing LLMs with deterministic validators or simulators and using generate–validate–repair loops—can improve adherence to constraints on curated tasks, but reported gains depend strongly on verifier fidelity, sampling semantics, and repair policies. Studies of guardrails, schema‑based tool interfaces, and red‑teaming highlight trade‑offs between reduced unsafe acceptance and increased false refusals or operator burden; authors therefore advocate workflow‑centred, replayable, sandboxed evaluations and ROC‑style diagnostics for verifier behaviour. Our study aligns with these recommendations by preregistering a paired estimand, using deterministic synthetic tasks and a sandboxed validator, and archiving full validator traces and execution manifests to enable reproducible diagnosis.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as cand-2026-01-prereg-v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on binary SAFE indicators produced by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Confirmatory test: exact two‑sided McNemar; paired bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). Design and sampling. A deterministic task generator produced N=200 synthetic intent→configuration tasks constrained to IPv4 reachability, ACL/filtering, and limited fields (admin, mtu, vlan). Tasks included explicit initial_state, expected_final_state and required_sequence workflow policies. The preregistration allowed two generation semantics: independent per‑arm generation (one LLM call per arm per task) or shared_initial_candidate (one LLM call per task whose candidate is scored by both arms). Model and pipeline. Declared model: gpt-5-mini; orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performing full_intent_constraint_validation (deterministic sandboxed scoring, outputs structured traces and a binary valid flag). The preregistered execution_contract included a planned maximum_model_calls of 400 for independent per‑arm generation; the executed run used shared_initial_candidate semantics (independent_condition_generation = false) and consumed model_calls_used = 200. Scoring and analysis. Each candidate was scored by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and encoded as SAFE (1) if validator.valid = true, UNSAFE (0) otherwise. Paired_binary_analysis_v1 computed contingency counts (n11,n10,n01,n00), exact McNemar two‑sided p, and paired bootstrap CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). Missingness, retry, and exclusion rules from the preregistration were applied deterministically; no technical failures or exclusions occurred in the confirmatory set. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the supplied bundle (execution/* and analysis/*) for deterministic replay.
sections.results: Execution accounting. The execution manifest records completed_episode_count = 400 (200 paired episodes), failed_episode_count = 0 and model_calls_used = 200 consistent with shared_initial_candidate semantics; provider audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 200. Confirmatory outcomes. The deterministic validator labeled every confirmatory candidate as SAFE: baseline SAFE successes = 200/200 and guarded SAFE successes = 200/200. The resulting paired contingency counts are n11 = 200 (SAFE in both arms), n10 = 0 (SAFE guarded only), n01 = 0 (SAFE baseline only), n00 = 0 (UNSAFE in both). From these counts the paired SAFE‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) equals 0.0. Statistical outputs (paired_binary_analysis_v1): exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Representative traces and repairs. Representative scoring JSONs show that shared_initial_candidate content was identical across baseline and guarded episodes and that validator.violation_count = 0 with validator.valid = true in every confirmatory trace. repair_provider_trace fields are null in all confirmatory scoring JSONs, indicating that no automatic repairs were invoked during confirmatory episodes. Missingness and contamination. Analysis artifacts report complete_pairs = 200 and no flagged or excluded episodes; the preregistered exploratory reserve (up to 50 tasks) intended for ROC/refusal calibration was not consumed before confirmatory execution.
sections.discussion: Why the inferential test was uninformative. The inferential degeneracy arises from three archived facts that jointly make the preregistered paired contrast mechanically untestable: (1) generation semantics executed as shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false), so exactly one LLM candidate per task was used for both arms (execution/model_configuration.json and execution/execution_manifest.json); (2) deterministic_netops_validator_v5 labeled every sampled candidate as valid (validator.valid = true in execution/scoring/*.json); and (3) no repairs were applied in confirmatory episodes (repair_provider_trace = null in scoring JSONs). With identical per‑pair candidates and no guarded‑arm modifications, discordant pairs (n10 or n01) cannot arise and McNemar’s test has no discordant evidence to act on, producing p = 1.0 and a degenerate CI. Diagnostic implications. This outcome does not demonstrate that the guarded pipeline is safe in production; it demonstrates a failure of testability under the executed design choices and model outputs. The preregistered power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline unsafe rate (~10–15%) and discordant-pair proportions; those assumptions were violated because the adversarial transforms used here did not elicit unsafe outputs from the declared model under the sampled tasks and because shared generation removed per‑arm stochasticity. Design recommendations for informative repeats (artifact‑grounded): (a) use independent per‑arm generation when the estimand is the causal effect of adding a verifier (requires ~400 model calls vs executed 200; see execution/execution_manifest.json); (b) consume a preregistered exploratory reserve (we reserved up to 50 tasks) to calibrate adversarial transforms until baseline unsafe rates match power assumptions, then freeze transforms before confirmatory execution; (c) if repairs are part of the guarded pipeline, instrument and archive repair_provider_trace artifacts and quantify UNSAFE→SAFE conversions and any introduced violations; (d) include a deterministic pilot check before committing the full confirmatory run and abort to contingency‑preserving preregistered paths if pilot shows ceiling/floor contingencies. Threats to validity and operational caveats. Internal validity is affected by generation semantics and model budgeting choices; construct validity is limited by the synthetic task scope (fields limited to admin/mtu/vlan) and by validator completeness; external validity is constrained by single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic topologies; conclusion validity under the executed run is null for the preregistered causal estimand because discordant pairs were absent. Reproducibility. All numerical summaries, contingency tables, scoring JSONs, and logs are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, execution/scoring/*.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl) and permit deterministic replay of the executed, non‑informative outcome. Investigators seeking an informative repeat should consult these artifacts before changing preregistered design choices.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully archived preregistered paired experiment comparing gpt‑5‑mini baseline generation and a deterministic verifier‑augmented pipeline on 200 synthetic NetOps tasks. Under the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics and for the declared model, both arms produced zero verifier‑detected unsafe proposals (paired difference = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]). Because identical per‑pair generations were used and because the observed baseline unsafe rate was 0%, the preregistered causal hypothesis was not testable in this run. The contribution is therefore methodological and reproducibility‑centred: (1) a complete deterministic preregistered run with archived artifacts that permit exact replay; (2) an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why this execution was non‑informative; and (3) concrete, archive‑supported recommendations (independent per‑arm generation budgeting, adversarial calibration, and exploratory ROC estimation) that preserve preregistration integrity and enable informative repeats.

limitations: Synthetic tasks and scope: tasks were deterministic synthetic topologies produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and limited to single‑AS, multi‑device setups; results may not generalize to production, multi‑AS, or vendor‑specific features.

Generation semantics: the executed run used shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false), producing identical per‑pair generations and creating a ceiling effect when shared candidates were valid.

Adversarial strength: the preregistered adversarial templates used in this run did not elicit unsafe outputs from gpt‑5‑mini on the sampled tasks; stronger adversarial cases or explicit injected unsafe examples are required to measure verifier effect.
Single‑model scope: only the declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) was evaluated; no multi‑model generality is claimed.

Verifier completeness: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 ran deterministically in synthetic sandboxed states; external validation of validator completeness against all real‑world NetOps failure modes is not provided.

Operational external validity: no production deployment, operator‑in‑the‑loop workload measurement, nor multi‑vendor field trials were performed; operator‑cost trade‑offs remain unquantified at scale.
